name: HTTP / REST APIs
description: Understand the web’s contract: methods, status codes, and request semantics.

questions.question: Which method is defined as idempotent by HTTP semantics?
questions.explanation: Repeating the same PUT should have the same intended server effect as sending it once.

questions.question: Which of these HTTP methods are idempotent by specification?
questions.explanation: GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent. POST has no general idempotency guarantee.

questions.question: An idempotent request must return an identical status code every time.
questions.explanation: Idempotency concerns the intended server effect, not identical responses. Repeated DELETE requests may return different statuses.

questions.question: Which status code indicates that a request created one or more resources?
questions.explanation: 201 Created indicates successful creation of one or more resources.

questions.question: Which of these methods are defined as safe?
questions.explanation: Safe methods have essentially read-only requested semantics. Incidental effects such as logging are still possible.

questions.question: A 204 response includes a response content body.
questions.explanation: 204 No Content ends after the header section and cannot contain content or trailers.

questions.question: Which header describes the media type of request or response content?
questions.explanation: Content-Type identifies the media type of the associated representation.

questions.question: Which request header expresses acceptable response media types?
questions.explanation: Accept lets a client describe which response media types it can accept.

questions.question: HEAD has GET semantics except that the server does not send response content.
questions.explanation: HEAD requests representation metadata without transferring the response content.

questions.question: Which status codes are in the client-error class?
questions.explanation: The 4xx class indicates client errors; 5xx indicates server errors.

questions.question: Which header commonly identifies the primary resource created in a 201 response?
questions.explanation: A Location field in a 201 response identifies the primary resource created by the request.

questions.question: A 202 Accepted response guarantees that processing will ultimately succeed.
questions.explanation: 202 means processing was accepted but has not completed; it does not guarantee the eventual outcome.
